limitations: Development only. Deduplicating exactly coincident nominal ghost boxes is a tested diagnostic, not a validated fix or a change to the frozen criteria.
Missing colors do not alone establish invisibility of a RAM slot, especially with blue/frightened ghosts or occlusion.
No reserved data or ROM opened; no new emulated frames.

This ad hoc read-only analysis used stdin scripts, which were not saved as source artifacts. The report records inputs, algorithms, counts and concrete witnesses but is not an executable replay script.
The explicit previous-RAM result is a phase diagnostic; it is not authorization to replace the existing raw fixture contract or to claim 99 percent calibration.

findings: Frames 1-3: orange/cyan/pink slots share exactly the same cage position while one visible colour cycles cyan,orange,pink; red is separately visible. RAM logical slots cannot all count as simultaneously visible objects.
Deduplicating exact positions and changing width 9 to 8 improves agreement only to 2895/8192 and geometry 16696/19596. It is insufficient and is not proposed as a completed fix.

For normal colours with one connected component, dominant exact 8x10 positions total 17130 with preceding RAM from the same episode, versus 11194 with current RAM. The latter includes episode-first frames; the former excludes them. These are descriptive exact-box counts, not matched-denominator calibration fractions. They support a one-frame render/game-state phase difference.
First independent disappearance at 285: red is absent although spatially separated from other ghost boxes; it reappears 286. A spatial overlap rule alone cannot model display selection.

All five ghost palettes are absent in 463 frames; first 858, during a post-collision sequence with logical coordinates retained. At 857 RAM25 becomes 0 while ghosts are still visible; at 858 they are absent. This is a witness of phase sensitivity, not proof that RAM25 alone universally controls visibility.
432 frames contain frightened-blue pixels. Absence of a normal colour does not establish absence of that allocation slot. Multiple blue components must remain supported.

The RGB baseline reports more than four ghosts in 67 frames. At 815 two red 1x1 components lie entirely inside another red 8x10 envelope. They may be disconnected ghost pixels or red player detail; contained islands do not justify additional ghost targets.

Common visible body is 8x10; 8x9 boxes shifted down one pixel also occur. The proposed 8x10 nominal body already tolerates that one-edge difference. Larger contact or clipped shapes remain uncalibrated.
minimal_next_steps: Keep original V0 baseline FAIL and all 8192 frames. Use a new development candidate with unchanged 99 percent/minimum 50 criteria.

RGB-only correction to test: absorb same-colour connected components whose boxes are wholly contained in another plausible ghost envelope, without using RAM or choosing targets from reference predictions. Preserve separate blue bodies; do not globally keep one component per colour or discard all small visible fragments.

RAM geometry candidate: use explicit pre-act or previous ordinary-frame logical coordinates, x=RAM[6+slot]-12,y=RAM[12+slot]+1,width8,height10. The first frame after cold construction needs an explicit pre-act RAM source or declared bounded fallback; do not silently shift labels across episodes or exclude first frames.

Renderer visibility selection remains an open blocker. Derive it independently from a justified RAM/render-state rule before scoring. Neither deduplication, current RAM47>0, normal-colour absence, nor filtering RAM labels by this same RGB checker is sufficient.

Test the fixed phase and visibility candidate on the full existing development capture, then on prospectively declared coverage for frightened/contacts if needed; reserved 17412 stays closed until candidate and protocol are fixed.
